newsitem.title: UK: NWE diesel cargoes firm on supply, barges dull.
newsitem.headline: NWE diesel cargoes firm on supply, barges dull.

text.p: Supply tightness firmed premiums for NWE low sulphur diesel cargoes on Wednesday while those for heating oil were firm on lack of prompt shipping, traders said.
Prompt low sulphur diesel was assessed at Feb +$19/20, around $3 firmer than the Feb IPE +$16 done on Tuesday for the end of January. February 1-10 dates were around Feb IPE +$17.
Feb IPE gas oil futures gained $2.50 to $206.25 a tonne due to a technical correction after heavy selling on Tuesday.
Diesel supply is tight because of refiners' preference for heating oil production during freezing weather early in the month, leading to a late month shortfall.
Prompt heating oil cargoes were around Feb IPE +$12/14 cif Le Havre with German quality around Feb IPE +$9 cif Hamburg.
Barges were thinly-traded because of continuing delivery problems along ice-jammed inland waterways.
Slacker demand depressed by the transport problems and warmer weather lowered prompt heating oil by around 50 cents, trading at Feb IPE +$5.50 and +$6 fob Rotterdam.
Heating oil traded at Feb +$3.50 for February 1-10. Low sulphur diesel was notionally Feb IPE +$13/14.
